outcome: The general closed curve problem (explicit necessary and sufficient conditions on periodic curvature and torsion for a space curve to close up) remains open, but Bamba and Ogata (Journal of Geometry, 2026) gave an explicit constructive solution for the special case of rotationally symmetric (spherical) curves, and extended it to closed curves with singularities (closed planar Legendre curves, closed spherical fronts).
summary: Wikipedia's bullet asks for explicit necessary and sufficient conditions on two periodic functions (curvature and torsion, or curvature alone in the plane case) so that the associated integral (Frenet) curve is closed. This is a long-standing open problem in the differential geometry of curves. Prior to the frozen revision, Grinevich and Schmidt (1990s work, well before the window) had already given a characterization of the closure constraints in terms of the spectral problem for an associated 2x2 matrix differential (Zakharov-Shabat/AKNS-type) operator arising from the self-focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation — a structural/spectral characterization, not an 'explicit' closed-form condition, so the problem as Wikipedia poses it (explicit conditions) remained open going into 2024. Searching for developments in the window, I found one clearly relevant, dated result: Bamba and Ogata, 'Closed space curves with singularities, generated by periodic curvature and torsion,' Journal of Geometry 117, article 12, published online 2026-02-02 (DOI 10.1007/s00022-025-00792-3; the '025' in the DOI indicates acceptance in 2025). No arXiv preprint of this paper could be located, so the journal publication is treated as the first written argument. The paper gives a constructive method for generating closed curves by controlling only the values of the first integral of a periodic function, which in turn determines periodic curvature and torsion; this yields an explicit solution to the closed curve problem for the restricted class of rotationally symmetric (spherical) curves, and the authors extend the construction to curves with singularities (closed planar Legendre curves and closed spherical fronts). This is a genuine restriction of the stated problem — a class of curves (rotationally symmetric/spherical), not a changed problem — so under Sec 3.1 it is a case of the problem and I classify it as 'partial' with resolution_direction 'confirmed' (the case was settled, not refuted). The fully general problem (arbitrary periodic curvature and torsion pairs in R^3, or arbitrary periodic curvature for plane curves) is still open; I found no other result in the window (2024-01-26 to 2026-09-22) that advances the general case, and no AI involvement of any kind — I checked the Springer abstract/search summaries, related arXiv papers on closed space curves (e.g. 'Unsigned Frenet Data of Closed Space Curves', arXiv:2608.09194, which explicitly addresses a different problem — the inverse problem of recovering signed torsion from unsigned data — and discloses no AI use), and general searches for AI-assisted solutions to this specific problem, none of which turned up any AI system credited in this area. I could not access the full text of the Bamba-Ogata paper (Springer paywall redirected to a login page, and a related Hokkaido University seminar PDF could not be parsed as text), so I relied on search-engine summaries and abstracts of the paper rather than the full manuscript; this is a limitation noted in 'incomplete'.
competing_reading: One could argue the plane-curve version of this problem (a single periodic curvature function determining a closed plane curve) is a genuinely separate sub-problem from the space-curve version (curvature and torsion), since Wikipedia's phrasing ('two periodic functions') most naturally reads as the space-curve case, but the plane case is the classical, well-studied one (e.g. 'When Is a Periodic Function the Curvature of a Closed Plane Curve?', pre-2024, unrelated to this window). If the bullet is read as covering only the space-curve problem, the Bamba-Ogata paper is squarely on-point as a special case; if read to also require progress on the plane case, no additional plane-curve progress was found in the window, which would not change the 'partial' classification since the space-curve special case alone already justifies it, but would narrow what 'partial' rests on.
what_would_settle_it: Direct access to the full text of Bamba and Ogata (2026) to confirm the precise scope of 'rotationally symmetric' curves covered, and a systematic search of 2024-2026 arXiv listings in math.DG for any paper that advances the fully general closed curve problem (not just a subclass) or credits an AI system with any part of the argument.

events.what: Bamba and Ogata give a constructive method producing closed curves from periodic curvature and torsion, giving an explicit solution for rotationally symmetric (spherical) curves, extended to planar Legendre curves and spherical fronts

judgement.doubts: The record never opened the Bamba–Ogata paper; its scope ('explicit solution for rotationally symmetric curves') comes from search-engine summaries. The singular-curve extensions (Legendre curves, fronts) are variants, not cases of the bullet; the partial status rests on the spherical/rotationally symmetric smooth class. If the full text showed the method only generates examples rather than giving necessary-and-sufficient conditions for a class, this would drop to none and the status to open. The Grinevich–Schmidt spectral characterization is pre-snapshot and not explicit, so it does not make this open_stale.
